title: Buildpacks Move the Container Hardening Control Point Away From the Dockerfile
gist: Cloud Native Buildpacks (CNCF-graduated 17 July 2026) relocate base-image choice and CVE patch cadence from per-repo Dockerfiles to a platform-owned builder, where the rebase command swaps OS layer digests in milliseconds instead of triggering a full rebuild per service. With Docker's hardened image catalogue free under Apache 2.0 since December 2025 and Docker Select and BellSoft Standard both committing to 7-day critical-CVE remediation, image-level differentiation is commoditising and value shifts to who maintains, signs and promotes the builder.

themes.theme: Control point moves from Dockerfile to builder

insights.claim: Cloud Native Buildpacks relocate base image selection and patch cadence from individual application teams to platform engineering, making the platform team the entity that determines how quickly a critical CVE is remediated across a fleet of hundreds of services.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Security budget and tooling spend migrates from per-team scanning/remediation seats toward a small number of platform-level builder vendors; vendors selling per-developer container security may face seat compression.
insights.quote: Cloud Native Buildpacks move those decisions to platform engineering, deciding how quickly a critical CVE is remediated across a fleet of hundreds of services.
insights.locator: Where a Dockerfile leaves base image

insights.claim: Because a Dockerfile declares its base in a FROM line inside every repository, propagating a patched base requires changing every service, and automation tools like Renovate and Dependabot only automate the edit, not the resulting full build, CI queue slot, test run and redeploy multiplied by the number of services.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: The real cost of Dockerfile-based patching is CI compute and change-management throughput, not the dependency-bot subscription — a bullish read for CI capacity consumption and a bearish one for the 'bots solved patching' narrative.
insights.quote: Renovate and Dependabot automate the mechanical part, but they cannot remove the rebuild: every updated FROM line still triggers a full build, a CI queue slot, a test run and a redeploy, multiplied by the number of services.
insights.locator: The difference lies in where the base image is declared

insights.claim: The Cloud Native Buildpacks project graduated within the CNCF on 17 July 2026, giving the model the maturity signal enterprises typically require before standardising a build toolchain.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Graduation is the usual trigger for enterprise procurement of commercial distributions around a project — watch buildpack-adjacent vendors for a post-graduation adoption step-up.
insights.locator: The Cloud Native Buildpacks project, which graduated

insights.claim: The stated organisational rationale for buildpacks is to concentrate container build best-practice knowledge inside a specialised team rather than have application developers across the organisation each maintain their own Dockerfiles.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: A centralisation framework that applies beyond containers: any org-wide security control with per-repo declaration is a candidate for the same platform-team consolidation and the same vendor-capture dynamic.
insights.quote: concentrate the knowledge of container build best practices within a specialized team, instead of having application developers across the organization individually maintain their own Dockerfiles.
insights.locator: frames this as a way to

themes.theme: Rebase economics vs the rebuild cycle

insights.claim: A buildpack builder is an OCI image packaging an ordered set of buildpacks, the lifecycle and a build-time base image, plus a metadata reference to a separate runtime 'run image', which is the structural separation that lets existing compatible application images be rebased without rebuilding application layers.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: The build-time/run-time base split is the technical moat of the model; any vendor product that merges or extends the run image forfeits it, which is the key diligence question when evaluating hardened-builder offerings.
insights.quote: A builder is an OCI image packaging an ordered set of buildpacks, the lifecycle and a build-time base image, together with a reference to a separate runtime base image, the "run image", held as metadata.

insights.claim: The rebase command detects a newer runtime base image and rewrites the OCI manifest and configuration, swapping OS layer digests for those of the new run image and bypassing the rebuild cycle entirely.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Patch propagation becomes a metadata write rather than a compute job, collapsing the marginal cost of fleet-wide OS remediation to near zero — a structural deflation of CI spend for orgs that adopt it.
insights.quote: Swapping the OS layer digests for those of the new run image bypasses the rebuild cycle entirely.
insights.locator: The mechanism is the rebase command

insights.claim: Joe Kutner, writing for the CNCF TAG Environmental Sustainability group in December 2023, characterised rebase as essentially an edit to a JSON file taking milliseconds and very little compute, with no rebuild, source access or CI queue required.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: The 'no source access' property matters for vendored or archived services whose build environments no longer reproduce — rebase patches images teams can no longer rebuild at all.
insights.quote: essentially an edit to a JSON file, taking milliseconds and very little compute, with no rebuild, source access or CI queue
insights.locator: Writing for the CNCF TAG Environmental Sustainability group

insights.claim: Rebase only replaces compatible run-image layers, so vulnerabilities living in application dependencies still require a full rebuild — the millisecond path covers the OS layer only, not the whole CVE surface.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Bounds the addressable share of remediation: buildpacks compress OS-layer patching but leave the dependency-layer market (SCA, dependency scanning) intact.
insights.quote: Rebase only replaces compatible run-image layers; vulnerabilities in application dependencies still require a rebuild.
insights.locator: Rebase only replaces compatible run-image layers

insights.claim: Even with rebase, updating production still requires testing, promotion and deployment, so the millisecond figure describes image mutation rather than end-to-end time-to-remediation in a regulated delivery pipeline.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Discount vendor time-to-patch marketing: the binding constraint on real MTTR becomes change approval and promotion, which is where deployment-orchestration tooling captures value.
insights.quote: though updating production still requires testing, promotion and deployment
insights.locator: Subsequent builds pick up a new run image

insights.claim: BellSoft announced general availability on 21 July 2026 of a hardened Paketo builder built on its Alpaquita Linux-based Hardened Images, replacing both the build and run stacks with a reduced package set, non-root defaults, signatures and SBOM data.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Marks the start of vendor competition at the builder layer rather than the base-image layer; watch whether Chainguard and Docker ship equivalent builder-level products in response.
insights.locator: BellSoft announced general availability on 21 July 2026

insights.claim: BellSoft itself describes patches reaching applications 'on the next build' rather than through rebase, meaning the millisecond patching path is a property of the buildpacks model and not something the vendor is contractually delivering.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: A concrete gap between model capability and vendor deliverable — buyers should test whether a hardened builder actually preserves rebase-ability before paying for the speed story.
insights.quote: BellSoft itself describes patches reaching applications "on the next build" rather than through rebase, so the millisecond path is a property of the model rather than a vendor claim.
insights.locator: BellSoft itself describes patches reaching applications

insights.claim: BellSoft states a patched image is published typically within 24 hours of disclosure, but its contractual Standard tier only advertises a 7-day remediation SLA for critical vulnerabilities and 14 days for all others, while the free Community tier lists no SLA at all.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: The gap between marketed 24-hour publication and the 7-day contractual commitment is the real risk transfer being sold; price the SLA, not the marketing number.
insights.quote: It states that a patched image is published "typically within 24 hours" of disclosure; contractually, its Standard tier advertises a 7-day remediation SLA for critical vulnerabilities and 14 days for all others
insights.locator: It states that a patched image is published

insights.claim: Docker made its entire hardened image catalogue free under an Apache 2.0 licence in December 2025 while retaining paid tiers for SLA-backed remediation, and Docker's Select tier commits to remediating critical CVEs within seven days, exactly matching BellSoft's Standard tier.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Free catalogues plus converging SLAs means the hardened-image product itself no longer sustains pricing power — revenue must come from support, attestation and accountability, compressing margins for pure-play image vendors.
insights.quote: Docker made its entire hardened image catalogue free under an Apache 2.0 licence in December 2025, retaining paid tiers for SLA-backed remediation.
insights.locator: Other vendors including Chainguard, Docker, Wiz and Minimus

insights.claim: With Chainguard, Docker, Wiz and Minimus all competing on low- or zero-CVE image catalogues while prices fall to free and SLAs converge, differentiation moves to delivery and accountability, which is the argument for treating the builder rather than the image as the commercial control point.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Positioning signal for the container-security sector: value accrues to whoever owns the build and promotion pipeline, not whoever ships the cleanest base image.
insights.quote: If the images are free and the SLAs converge, differentiation moves to delivery and accountability, which is the argument for treating the builder, not the image, as the control point.
insights.locator: If the images are free and the SLAs converge

insights.claim: A BellSoft survey of 250 Spring developers, tech leads and architects at Spring I/O 2026 found 64% did not recognise their Dockerfile as a security risk.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Awareness, not tooling, is the binding constraint on Dockerfile hygiene — implies a long adoption runway for platform-mandated builders since developers will not self-select into the fix.
insights.quote: found that 64% did not recognise their Dockerfile as a security risk
insights.locator: BellSoft’s own survey of 250 Spring developers

insights.claim: A cross-tag study of 6,292 Docker images presented at ICSME 2025 found nearly 61% of repositories carried vulnerable application dependencies in every tag examined, meaning the vulnerability was never fixed in any published version.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Quantifies the addressable market for automated remediation, but note these are application-layer findings that rebase explicitly does not solve — a persistent gap for SCA vendors to own.
insights.quote: a cross-tag study of 6,292 Docker images (ICSME 2025) found nearly 61% of repositories carried vulnerable application dependencies in every tag examined
insights.locator: Patch discipline is weak more broadly

insights.claim: Buildpacks trade away the step-by-step control of hand-written Dockerfiles and are awkward for workloads needing custom OS packages or language ecosystems the buildpacks do not cover, so they are not a universal replacement.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Caps the realistic penetration of the model — expect hybrid estates and therefore continued demand for Dockerfile-based scanning alongside builder-based platforms.
insights.quote: They trade away the step-by-step control of hand-written Dockerfiles, which is awkward for workloads needing custom OS packages or language ecosystems the buildpacks do not cover.
insights.locator: Buildpacks are not a universal fix

insights.claim: Image extensions let platform teams generate build.Dockerfile and run.Dockerfile steps inside an otherwise standard buildpack build, but extending the run image can compromise rebase-ability, so teams buy back Dockerfile-style control at the price of the fast patching path that made the model attractive.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: The escape hatch silently destroys the core benefit — a diligence checkpoint when assessing whether an organisation's buildpack adoption will actually deliver the claimed remediation speed.
insights.quote: but extending the run image can compromise rebase-ability, so teams buy back Dockerfile-style control at the cost of the fast patching path that made the model attractive.
insights.locator: Image extensions close much of that gap

insights.claim: Buildpacks can mean slower cold builds and larger images and concentrate trust in the platform builder, framing the decision as control versus blast radius, with governance shifting to whoever maintains, signs and promotes the builder under rising pressure from regulations like the EU Cyber Resilience Act.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Regulatory forcing function pushes value toward signing, attestation and provenance tooling attached to the builder, while centralised remediation speed also centralises the single point of compromise.
insights.quote: The choice is control versus blast radius
insights.locator: Buildpacks can also mean slower cold builds
